input.quote: 15.5 Governing Law. This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York without reference to any rules of conflict of laws.
input.rationale: Governing law meets the preferred position exactly: New York law with conflicts rules disclaimed (Section 15.5, p0627). The dispute forum is not walk-away territory - Section 15.6(a) provides for arbitration administered by JAMS, a US-domestic administrator, under its Comprehensive Rules, rather than foreign-seated arbitration or exclusive venue in a counterparty home jurisdiction outside the accepted list. The framework is court-supported and US-anchored: judgment on the award may be entered in any court having jurisdiction (p0630); patent and trademark scope, validity and infringement disputes are carved out to a court of competent jurisdiction in the country of grant (Section 15.6(h), p0637); Program Invention ownership is adjudicated under U.S. patent law (p0638); and either Party retains access to a court for interim and equitable relief before or during arbitration (Section 15.6(j), p0639). Good-faith escalation to the JSC and Designated Senior Officers (p0233) is a permitted pre-step, and the final decision-making power vested in Sanofi's Designated Senior Officer (p0234) benefits our party, so it is not flagged. Two sub-elements noted for the file rather than redlined: (i) the arbitral seat and arbitrator count are redacted ("arbitration in [***] before [***] arbitrators"), and we should confirm in diligence that the seat is New York or another accepted US location, since a foreign seat would convert this to a deviation; and (ii) the clause elects domestic arbitration rather than the preferred exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, which the playbook tolerates because it is not foreign arbitration.
